author: reek
body: Concurrency in anger: the event-loop WebServer holds TWO client connections at once and serves both, with their frames INTERLEAVED. Two clients on distinct source ports both connect to the serve port; the requests are fed A-SYN, B-SYN, A-ACK, B-ACK, A-GET, B-GET, so at the moment each GET arrives the OTHER client's connection is already open. Correct dispatch routes each GET to its own connection.

author: reek
body: The control is the request count per connection. Correct dispatch gives A=1, B=1. A broken demultiplex that always picked connection 0 would give A=2, B=0 -- the second client's request served on the first client's connection. That is exactly the lost-request failure 4.20 is about, made visible.

author: reek
body: One frame is one request here (no reassembly), and the GET is a separate frame from the handshake ACK because a data segment arriving in SYN_RECEIVED is consumed as the ACK that establishes the connection and its payload is dropped -- a real property of the raw path, worked around by the client retransmitting.
